title: Vodafone Idea Q2 Loss Widens After One-Off Charge, ARPU Rises
excerpt: For the quarter ended September 30, 2026, Vodafone Idea's reported net loss widened to Rs 5,975 crore after a Rs 462 crore exceptional charge, even as its pre-exceptional loss narrowed and ARPU rose to Rs 198.
body:
• For the quarter ended September 30, 2026 (Q2 FY27), Vodafone Idea reported a net loss of Rs 5,975 crore, wider than Rs 5,524 crore a year earlier, after a Rs 462 crore exceptional charge.
  • Revenue from operations rose 6.2% year on year to Rs 11,884 crore, narrowly below the Rs 11,896 crore average analyst estimate compiled by LSEG, according to Reuters.
  • Average revenue per user rose 9.7% year on year to Rs 198, helped by growth in 4G and 5G users and a 27% rise in data usage.
  • The pre-exceptional loss narrowed slightly, so the charge explains the wider headline loss.

Vodafone Idea reported its results for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 — the second quarter of its 2026-27 financial year — on Thursday, November 12, 2026. The figures were reported by the company and covered by Reuters and The Hindu BusinessLine. The quarter contains two loss numbers moving in opposite directions.

Reported figures, period first

For Q2 FY27, Vodafone Idea's consolidated loss after tax was Rs 5,975 crore, according to BusinessLine, compared with a loss of Rs 5,524 crore in the same quarter a year earlier. Reuters reported the same after-tax figure in rupees as 59.75 billion rupees, and noted that it was adjusted for a one-off charge of about 4.6 billion rupees.

On a pre-tax basis, Reuters reported that the consolidated loss narrowed to 54.99 billion rupees (Rs 5,499 crore) in the quarter ended September 30, from 55.65 billion rupees a year earlier. BusinessLine put the loss excluding the exceptional item at Rs 5,513 crore, marginally lower than Rs 5,562 crore in the year-ago quarter. That distinction is the core of the story: before the exceptional item, the loss narrowed slightly; after it, the reported net loss widened.

The exceptional item itself was a loss of Rs 462 crore. BusinessLine said the higher reported loss was primarily due to an adverse mark-to-market impact on treasury assets, classified as an exceptional item, arising from the remeasurement of settlement assets.

Reported versus expected

Expectations should be kept separate from reported results. On revenue, Reuters said overall revenue rose about 6.2% to 118.84 billion rupees (Rs 11,884 crore), narrowly missing analysts' average estimate of 118.96 billion rupees (Rs 11,896 crore), per data compiled by LSEG. Neither Reuters nor BusinessLine, in the reporting read for this article, gave a comparable consensus estimate for the net loss, so no loss-versus-estimate comparison is made here.

BusinessLine reported that revenue from operations rose 6.2% year on year and 1.7% sequentially to Rs 11,884 crore, from Rs 11,689 crore in Q1 FY27, driven by growth in service revenue and trading goods. EBITDA stood at Rs 4,981 crore, up 6.3% from a year ago, although it declined slightly from Rs 5,034 crore in the preceding quarter, BusinessLine said. Reuters said total expenses rose 5.3%, led by higher finance and roaming costs.

The driver: more revenue per user

Average revenue per user (ARPU), a key telecom metric, rose 9.7% year on year to Rs 198 in the quarter, Reuters reported, helped by a 2.5% increase in its 4G and 5G user base and 27% growth in data usage. BusinessLine reported data consumption rose to 93.6 PB per day from 73.6 PB per day a year ago, a rise of 27.1%, and that the 4G/5G subscriber base rose to 131 million, compared with 127.8 million a year earlier.

The total user base rose to 194.4 million as of September-end, from 193.1 million as of June-end, Reuters reported. BusinessLine noted that the total remained lower than 196.7 million reported a year ago. Reuters also noted that the June quarter marked Vodafone Idea's first quarterly sequential net subscriber addition since the 2018 Vodafone India-Idea merger.

Network spending and funding

BusinessLine reported that Vodafone Idea extended 5G services to 400 cities and towns in the quarter and added nearly 9,000 broadband towers, its highest quarterly addition in nine quarters. It said capex orders worth over Rs 13,200 crore have been placed, of which nearly Rs 6,000 crore has been executed. Reuters said the company has been stepping up investment in its 4G and 5G networks to improve network quality and arrest subscriber losses, while seeking bank debt to fund its planned 450 billion-rupee capital spending.

As of September 30, 2026, BusinessLine reported, the company's bank debt stood at Rs 943 crore, while its cash and bank balance was Rs 5,470 crore. It said the company has secured funding of over Rs 10,500 crore during the first half of FY27, including more than Rs 4,000 crore of incremental bank funding raised in the second quarter.

What to watch

Whether ARPU can keep rising without losing users, whether total subscribers can return to year-ago levels, and whether the exceptional charge proves to be a one-off.
nri_angle: Diaspora investors tracking Indian telecom holdings get the reported-versus-expected distinction and the one-off charge behind the wider headline loss.
author: Diaspora Desk
